items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: That's Mercer, too, isn't it; "Things Ain'T What They Used To Be".

ctx.x: strike or ban, and the band couldn't play... They had all these live remotes going, and they couldn't play any ASCAP tunes on the radio during that period, so that's when they changed themes and a whole lot of new material came into the book that Billy wrote. Because Duke couldn't write anything at that point. That's also when a lot of things showed up by Mercer Ellington.
Oh, that's right. [SINGS REFRAIN OF "Things Ain'T What They Used To Be"]. That's Mercer, too, isn't it; "Things Ain'T What They Used To Be".

Well, that's when it suddenly appeared. And a lot of things came out with Mercer's byline, or Mercer's composer credit. But during that period from January 1st until I think October, no ASCAP music could be broadcast.
